Hooks and hashtags — four-day week, 2026-11-10
4 hooks, 3 angles, 6 hashtags in use; strongest: "61 companies tried it; 56 kept it"

## Hooks
1. "61 companies tried a four-day week for six months; 56 kept it." [1] — LinkedIn, X
2. "Revenue was flat." [1] — LinkedIn
3. "We did not give people Friday off. We took Friday's work away." [2] — LinkedIn, Instagram
4. Depending on who you ask, it worked or "could not be measured". [1][3] — X

## Angles
- The part-timer's four-day week — no result mentions them.
- The meeting cull as the real product — [2] mentions it in passing.
- The companies that went back — only [3] is sceptical.

## Hashtags
- LinkedIn: #fourdayweek (in use, [1]) · #futureofwork (in use, [1])
- X: #4dayweek (in use, [3]) · #productivity (in use, [3])
- Instagram: #fourdayweek (in use, [1]) · #worksmarter (in use, [2])

## Sources
1. Four-day week pilot results — https://example.org/pilot — 2026-10-30 — "56 of 61 companies will continue."
2. What the fifth day cost us — https://blog.example/fifth-day — 2026-11-04 — "We took Friday's work away."
3. The four-day week is a mirage — https://sceptic.example/mirage — 2026-11-02 — "Productivity could not be measured."
